questions.title: Corruption Reporting
questions.text: Corruption Reporting — The ability for users to report corruption by public servants or institutions on the national government portal. Either via a dedicated platform or mechanism for individuals to confidentially submit allegations or instances of corruption they have encountered
questions.what: The ability for users to report corruption by public servants or institutions on the national government portal. Either via a dedicated platform or mechanism for individuals to confidentially submit allegations or instances of corruption they have encountered
questions.why: Empowers people to hold government officials and institutions accountable, fosters transparency and integrity in governance, and contributes to the overall efforts to combat corruption within the public sector.

how.scoring_guidance: Indicative steps: 1. Develop a Reporting Mechanism: a. Create a dedicated online form or portal section specifically for reporting instances of corruption by public servants or institutions. 2. Ensure Anonymity and Confidentiality: a. Implement measures to protect the identity of individuals making reports. 3. Provide Clear Instructions: a. Offer guidance on how to complete the reporting form, including details on the types of corruption that can be reported, relevant evidence or documentation to include, and the submission process. 4. Establish Investigation Procedures: a. Define protocols for handling and investigating corruption reports. 5. Communicate Follow-up Actions: a. Keep users informed about the progress of their reports, provide updates on any investigations or disciplinary actions taken against implicated parties. For more information, check out the OECD’s Public Integrity Handbook
how.criteria_for_yes: Evidence found on the designated government portal satisfying the What specification.
how.criteria_for_no: No evidence found or feature unreachable within reasonable navigation.

questions.title: Calendar on e-participation activities
questions.text: Calendar on e-participation activities — The provision of information about any upcoming e-participation activities. E-participation initiatives are initiatives offered to engage people in discussions, decision-making and policy-making. These can be identified through announcement(s), a calendar, of upcoming online consultation, voting forums, surveys, polls, etc.
questions.what: The provision of information about any upcoming e-participation activities. E-participation initiatives are initiatives offered to engage people in discussions, decision-making and policy-making. These can be identified through announcement(s), a calendar, of upcoming online consultation, voting forums, surveys, polls, etc.
questions.why: Keeps people informed and engaged in decision-making, fostering transparency, inclusivity, and active civic involvement in shaping national policies and initiatives.

how.scoring_guidance: Indicative steps: 1. Centralized Platform: a. Create a dedicated section on the national website for e-participation or a separate portal. 2. Clear Announcements: a. Provide clear and concise announcements about upcoming e-participation activities. 3. Interactive Calendar: a. Maintain an interactive calendar displaying all scheduled e-participation events. 4. Various Participation Tools: a. State what tools can be used for e-participation, online forums, voting platforms, surveys, or polls. 5. Regular Updates: a. Keep the e-participation section or website updated. 6. Promotion and Outreach: a. Actively promote upcoming e-participation events.
how.criteria_for_yes: Evidence found on the designated government portal satisfying the What specification.
how.criteria_for_no: No evidence found or feature unreachable within reasonable navigation.

questions.title: Online tools for policy
questions.text: Online tools for policy — The provision of online tools available on the any government portal(s) to collect public opinion from people to inform policy deliberation processes. Possible tools include online fora, social media, online polls, online voting tools, online petition tools, chats, blogs.
questions.what: The provision of online tools available on the any government portal(s) to collect public opinion from people to inform policy deliberation processes. Possible tools include online fora, social media, online polls, online voting tools, online petition tools, chats, blogs.
questions.why: These tools facilitate active participation, ensuring diverse perspectives inform policy deliberations, fostering democratic governance and inclusive decision-making processes.

how.scoring_guidance: Indicative steps: 1. Select Online Forums: a. Host dedicated forums where people can discuss specific topics. 2. Social Media Platforms: a. Utilize social media channels to conduct polls and surveys. 3. Online Polls: a. Simple and quick, online polls on the government website can gauge public sentiment on various issues. 4. Online Voting Tools: a. Implement secure online voting systems for non-binding national decisions. 5. Online Petition Tools: a. Allow people to create and sign petitions online.

questions.title: Open government data portal
questions.text: Open government data portal — The provision of an open government data portal, on a national level portal or at any other government/ministry websites including Statistics offices. Open Data Portal means a sub-website within the Government Website, where Government datasets are made available to the public in machine readable format.
questions.what: The provision of an open government data portal, on a national level portal or at any other government/ministry websites including Statistics offices. Open Data Portal means a sub-website within the Government Website, where Government datasets are made available to the public in machine readable format.
questions.why: Crucial for promoting transparency, empowering individuals, and fostering innovation by providing easy access to valuable government datasets in a machine-readable format.

how.scoring_guidance: Indicative steps: 1. Establish a Dedicated Portal: a. Create a separate section within the national government portal specifically or a dedicated government portal for hosting open government data. 2. Identify Relevant Datasets: a. Determine which government datasets are suitable for publication on the open data portal. 3. Ensure Data Accessibility: a. Publish datasets in machine-readable formats such as CSV, JSON, or XML to enable easy access. 4. Provide Metadata and Documentation: a. Accompany each dataset with comprehensive metadata and documentation, including descriptions, data dictionaries, and usage guidelines to enhance understanding and usability. 5. Implement Regular Updates: a. Commit to regularly updating and expanding the open data portal with new datasets and revisions.
how.criteria_for_yes: Evidence found on the designated government portal satisfying the What specification.

questions.title: New open datasets requests
questions.text: New open datasets requests — The ability for users to request new open datasets be made available online either on the data portal or elsewhere in government websites.
questions.what: The ability for users to request new open datasets be made available online either on the data portal or elsewhere in government websites.
questions.why: Essential for fostering collaboration between the government and individuals, promoting transparency, and ensuring that available data aligns with the needs and interests of the public.

how.scoring_guidance: Indicative steps: 1. Establish a Request Submission Mechanism: a. Implement a dedicated online form or portal section where users can submit requests for open datasets. 2. Define Submission Guidelines: a. Provide clear instructions on how users should submit their dataset requests. 3. Streamline Review and Approval Process: a. Develop a standardized procedure for reviewing and approving dataset requests, involving relevant government departments or agencies to assess feasibility and relevance. 4. Communicate Progress and Outcomes: a. Keep users informed about the status of their dataset requests, including updates on the review process, approvals, and timelines for dataset publication. 5. Act on User Feedback: a. Consider user feedback and requests as valuable input for prioritizing dataset releases and improving the overall openness and accessibility of government data.

questions.title: Open Datasets on government expenditures
questions.text: Open Datasets on government expenditures — Provision of open datasets related to national expenditures (budget) in PDF or Word (machine non-readable), or in open format (machine-readable) at any of the government portal(s).
questions.what: Provision of open datasets related to national expenditures (budget) in PDF or Word (machine non-readable), or in open format (machine-readable) at any of the government portal(s).
questions.why: Crucial for transparency, enabling residents to access vital financial data and policy documents easily, fostering accountability, and promoting an informed and engaged community.

how.scoring_guidance: Indicative steps: 1. Select Centralize Information: a. Create a dedicated section on the national website to house budgetary information and policy docs. b. Organize the content into clear categories such as annual budgets, financial reports, policy documents. 2. Regularly Update Content: a. Keep the online repository up-to-date with the latest budgetary allocations, financial reports, and policy changes. 3. Interactive Data Visualization: a. Utilize interactive charts, graphs, and infographics to visually represent budgetary data. 4. Feedback Mechanism: a. Integrate a feedback system where residents can ask questions or request additional information. 5. Promote Transparency: a. Clearly outline the country’s financial priorities, expenditure breakdowns, and policy. b. Include narratives and visualizations to explain how taxpayer funds are allocated and utilized.

Collect Feedback: a. Provide mechanisms for collecting feedback and input from participants during and after consultations.

questions.title: Participatory budgeting
questions.text: Participatory budgeting — The provision of participation possibility to the user regarding participatory budgeting or similar mechanism. Many countries around the world are starting to engage the people in the discussion of the country’s budget, known as "participatory budgeting".
questions.what: The provision of participation possibility to the user regarding participatory budgeting or similar mechanism. Many countries around the world are starting to engage the people in the discussion of the country’s budget, known as "participatory budgeting".
questions.why: Empowers people to engage in crucial discussions about the country’s financial allocations, fostering transparency, democratic decision-making, and people-driven development.

how.scoring_guidance: Indicative steps: 1. User-Friendly Interface: a. Design an intuitive online platform where people can easily access budget-related documents. 2. Transparency: a. Integrate social media platforms to create awareness about participatory budgeting events. 4. Online Surveys and Feedback Forms: a. Use online surveys and feedback forms to gather opinions and suggestions from people. 5. Clear Timelines: a. Publish clear timelines for the participatory budgeting process. 6. Regular Updates: a. Keep the website updated with progress reports, outcomes of participatory budgeting initiatives..

questions.title: E-participation portal(s)
questions.text: E-participation portal(s) — The provision of a dedicated e-participation portal available on any government website. This portal serves as a centralized hub where individuals can access information about ongoing consultations, provide feedback on policies and initiatives, participate in surveys or polls, and submit suggestions or ideas directly to government officials.
questions.what: The provision of a dedicated e-participation portal available on any government website. This portal serves as a centralized hub where individuals can access information about ongoing consultations, provide feedback on policies and initiatives, participate in surveys or polls, and submit suggestions or ideas directly to government officials.
questions.why: Promotes transparency, accountability, and democratic governance by direct citizen involvement in public affairs.

how.scoring_guidance: Indicative steps: 1. Establishment of a dedicated portal: a. Create a separate section within the government website specifically designated for e-participation. 2. Interactive features: a. Integrate interactive features such as discussion forums, polls, surveys, and suggestion boxes to encourage citizen engagement. 3. Accessible information: a. Ensure that the portal provides clear and comprehensive information about ongoing consultations, policies, and initiatives open for public input. 4. Notification system: a. Implement a system to alert users about new consultations, updates, and opportunities for engagement. 5. Feedback mechanisms: a. Develop mechanisms for people to provide feedback, suggestions, and comments on proposed policies and initiatives directly through the portal. For more info, check UN DESA’s 2020 UN E-Government Survey, Chapter 5 on e-participation

questions.title: Open data license
questions.text: Open data license — Evidence of information related to open data license on a national portal. A legal framework or agreement that governs the terms and conditions under which data can be accessed, used, and distributed. It outlines the rights and responsibilities of both data providers and users regarding the sharing and reuse of data.
questions.what: Evidence of information related to open data license on a national portal. A legal framework or agreement that governs the terms and conditions under which data can be accessed, used, and distributed. It outlines the rights and responsibilities of both data providers and users regarding the sharing and reuse of data.
questions.why: Crucial in promoting transparency, accountability, and innovation by facilitating the free flow of data while ensuring legal clarity and protection for all parties involved.

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Select Appropriate License: a. Choose a widely recognized open data license e.g. Creative Commons licenses or Open Data Commons. 2. Clearly Display License: a. Clearly display the chosen open data license alongside the datasets to inform users of their rights and obligations. 3. Provide License Details: a. Include detailed information about the terms and conditions of the open data license, such as permitted uses, attribution requirements, and any restrictions. 4. Offer License Options: a. Offer users the flexibility to select from different open data licenses based on their preferences and uses. 5. Ensure Compliance: a. Regularly review and update datasets to ensure they comply with the chosen open data license.

questions.title: Real time open government datasets
questions.text: Real time open government datasets — Evidence of real time open government dataset(s) in i) non-machine-readable (PDF, scanned files etc.) or ii) machine-readable (CSV, JSON, XML etc.). These datasets offer users timely insights into various aspects of government operations, policies, and services.
questions.what: Evidence of real time open government dataset(s) in i) non-machine-readable (PDF, scanned files etc.) or ii) machine-readable (CSV, JSON, XML etc.). These datasets offer users timely insights into various aspects of government operations, policies, and services.
questions.why: Enables transparency, accountability, and informed decision-making by allowing stakeholders to access and analyze relevant data in formats suitable for their needs.

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Establish Data Governance Framework: a. Develop policies and procedures for managing real-time open government datasets. 2. Implement Data Integration Tools: a. Utilize software tools and platforms to aggregate and integrate real-time data from various government sources into a centralized repository. 3. Ensure Data Accessibility: a. Design user-friendly interfaces and access points on government portals to enable easy retrieval and exploration of real-time datasets by the public. 4. Provide Data Documentation: a. Publish metadata and documentation alongside datasets to enhance understanding of data. 5. Promote Data Transparency: a. Regularly update and maintain real-time datasets to ensure accuracy, reliability, and relevance.

questions.title: Online services for rural areas
questions.text: Online services for rural areas — Evidence of online government service available to the people living in rural area with i) information, or ii) full online application at any of the government portal(s). Involves ensuring that people in rural communities have access to essential government services through digital platforms such as applying for permits, licenses, or benefits, accessing healthcare information, or participating in government programs
questions.what: Evidence of online government service available to the people living in rural area with i) information, or ii) full online application at any of the government portal(s). Involves ensuring that people in rural communities have access to essential government services through digital platforms such as applying for permits, licenses, or benefits, accessing healthcare information, or participating in government programs
questions.why: Ensures equitable access to government services for rural residents, promoting inclusivity and bridging the urban-rural digital divide.

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Identify Services: a. Determine essential government services needed by rural residents. 2. Develop Processes: a. Create user-friendly online application processes for identified services. 3. Provide Information: a. Ensure availability of information tailored to rural areas on government services. 4. Test Accessibility: a. Verify functionality and accessibility of online services in rural settings. 5. Promote Awareness: a. Conduct targeted outreach campaigns in rural communities to raise awareness of online services. For more info, check out OECD’s Guide on Implementing the Rural Well-being Policy Framework

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Designing User-Friendly Interface: a. Create an accessible and intuitive platform for submitting petitions. 2. Implementing Verification Measures: a. Develop a structured process for reviewing and responding to petitions, including acknowledgment and feedback timelines.

questions.title: Policy-decision making for vulnerable groups
questions.text: Policy-decision making for vulnerable groups — Evidence that people's voices were included, i.e. if their input was actually used in the policy decision-making on issues related to the following vulnerable groups (in the past 12 months), for immigrants, older people, persons living below poverty line, persons with disabilities, women, youth.
questions.what: Evidence that people's voices were included, i.e. if their input was actually used in the policy decision-making on issues related to the following vulnerable groups (in the past 12 months), for immigrants, older people, persons living below poverty line, persons with disabilities, women, youth.
questions.why: Vital for transparency and accountability, ensuring that government actions reflect the needs and perspectives of immigrants, older people, individuals living below the poverty line, persons with disabilities, women, and youth.

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Establish Dedicated Online Platforms: a. Create specific sections or portals on the government website for each vulnerable group. 2. Ensure Transparency: a. Publish summaries of consultations and highlight how input from vulnerable groups influenced policy decisions. 3. Provide Accessible Channels: a. Offer various channels for submitting feedback, including online surveys, forums, and email. 4. Regular Progress Updates: a. Update the portal regularly with progress reports on policy changes driven by public feedback from vulnerable groups. For more info, check out the OECD’s Lithuania guide Delivering for people in vulnerable situations.

questions.title: Online consultations for vulnerable groups
questions.text: Online consultations for vulnerable groups — Information on online consultations via forums, polls, questionnaires etc. to involve people among vulnerable groups in the past 12 months (for immigrants, older people, persons living below poverty line, persons with disabilities, women, youth), i.e. if actual consultations were held.
questions.what: Information on online consultations via forums, polls, questionnaires etc. to involve people among vulnerable groups in the past 12 months (for immigrants, older people, persons living below poverty line, persons with disabilities, women, youth), i.e. if actual consultations were held.
questions.why: Ensures transparency and accountability, indicating whether meaningful engagement occurred in policy discussions affecting these communities.

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Establish Dedicated Consultation Section: a. Create a dedicated section on the portal specifically for online consultations targeting vulnerable groups. 2. Promote Accessibility: a. Ensure that the consultation platform is accessible to all vulnerable groups, e.g. those with disabilities, providing options for various languages, easy navigation, and compatibility with assistive technologies. 3. Engage National Partners: a. Collaborate with national organizations and advocacy groups representing vulnerable populations to promote awareness of online consultations and encourage participation. 4. Provide Feedback Mechanism: a. Implement a feedback mechanism on the government portal where participants can provide input 5. Publicize Results: a. After the consultations, publish a summary of the feedback received and actions taken in response.
